page: Amazon Web Services r8i.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 32-vCPU configuration derived from 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading, the processor features 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a massive 480 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and AMX int8) alongside hardware encryption support via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 256.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It lacks dedicated local instance storage and contains zero GPUs, relying exclusively on network-attached storage via its 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier and strong performance in CPU-intensive tasks and compression pipelines. In single-threaded compression and decompression, gzip reached 33.51 GB/sec and bzip3 yielded 14.21 GB/sec, scaling to 223.94 GB/sec in multi-threaded decompression, placing it in the top 25%. Geekbench results showed strong execution with scores of 2,043.0 in single-core and 17,097.0 in multi-core tests, supported by high scores in image and text processing. PassMark metrics reflect strong computing capability, achieving an overall CPU score of 51,024.22 and an encryption test result of 36,285.59. Memory bandwidth reaches 2,556.75 GB/sec for cached 16 KB blocks and 133.67 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB read blocks.

For machine learning and web tasks, static web serving throughput reached a strong 55.37 GB/sec. CPU-based LLM inference demonstrated top-tier generation speed for small 135M models at 404.39 tokens/sec, and strong prompt processing for medium 7B models at 209.76 tokens/sec. However, processing larger 70B parameter models exhibits weaker generation performance at 2.71 tokens/sec, illustrating the throughput limitations of non-GPU architectures on heavy model inference. In-memory caching operations produced 58.27 million operations/sec on Redis SET benchmarks, falling within the middle 50% category alongside database operations scoring 14,978.72 on PassMark.

The r8i.8xlarge offers solid resource density for enterprise memory-bound workloads, balancing a high RAM capacity per core against modern DDR5 speeds and advanced vector computation capabilities. Given the lack of bundled local NVMe storage and discrete GPUs, this instance is best aligned with in-memory caching layers, medium-scale database workloads, data transformation pipelines, and CPU-driven batch processing tasks that require large footprints of fast memory.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 256.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (7 GHz), presenting an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains zero GPUs, and provides no local instance storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight strong performance in compression routines, PassMark CPU tests (51,024.22), Geekbench single-core (2,043.0) and multi-core (17,097.0) processing, and static web serving throughput (55.37 GB/sec). It also demonstrates top-tier token generation on lightweight LLM models, supported by AMX and AVX-512 extensions. The r8i.8xlarge is technically structured for in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, data transformation, and memory-intensive enterprise services.
